plain_english: When someone hurts you or insults you, remember this: they're acting based on what seems right to them. They can't follow what seems right to you — only what seems right to them. So if they're judging based on false impressions, they're the one getting hurt. They're the one being deceived. Think of it this way: if someone believes a true statement is false, the statement itself isn't damaged — only the person is fooled. With this in mind, you can calmly handle anyone who attacks you. Just tell yourself, "That's how it seemed to them."
original_excerpt: When any person does ill by you, or speaks ill of you, remember that he acts or speaks from an impression that it is right for him to do so. Now it is not possible that he should follow what appears right to you, but only what appears so to himself. Therefore, if he judges from false appearances, he is the person hurt, since he, too, is the person deceived. For if anyone takes a true proposition to be false, the proposition is not hurt, but only the man is deceived. Setting out, then, from these principles, you will meekly bear with a person who reviles you, for you will say upon every occasion, “It seemed so to him.”
